step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram features two main flows: a web security and analytics pipeline at the top and an instant payment processing flow at the bottom. 1. Incoming web traffic passes through AWS WAF to the EC2 web cluster. Suspicious IPs identified by EC2 are sent back to WAF for blocking. User and mobile mining data in RDS is periodically extracted by AWS Data Pipeline and pushed to Athena for gamified fraud detection analytics. 2. Mobile instant payments enter through API Gateway, triggering a Lambda function that evaluates the payment and records the status in DynamoDB.

graph.name: Electroneum Fraud Protection and Instant Payment Architecture
graph.notes: Electroneum uses a multi-layered security setup with WAF, EC2, Data Pipeline, and Athena to perform gamified fraud detection while using API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB for low-latency cryptocurrency instant payments.

nodes.name: WAF
nodes.notes: Filters incoming web traffic and applies IP blocking rules.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Web cluster processing legitimate traffic and detecting malicious actors using honey traps.

nodes.name: DATA PIPELINE
nodes.notes: Extracts user and mobile mining data for analytics.

nodes.name: ATHENA
nodes.notes: Performs post-analysis and gamified fraud rule evaluation.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Relational database storing user and mobile mining data.

nodes.name: API GATEWAY
nodes.notes: Entry point for instant payment requests from mobile devices.

nodes.name: LAMBDA
nodes.notes: Processes payment logic and verifies payment criteria.

nodes.name: DYNAMO
nodes.notes: Stores instant payment status outcomes (success or failure).

edges.notes: Filtered web traffic passes from WAF to EC2 instances.
EC2 feeds malicious IP addresses back to WAF for dynamic blocking.
User and mobile mining data sent from RDS into Data Pipeline.
Data Pipeline pushes processed data into Athena for analytical querying.
API Gateway routes instant payment requests to Lambda.
Lambda records transaction outcome status into DynamoDB.
